General Gordon Drummond ordered three failed frontal assaults on the enemy position during this engagement. Friendly fire happened again during this battle when Winfield Scott's forces were attacked by Americans. The British artillery was captured by James Miller during this battle. After winning this battle, the Americans moved to Fort Erie, but the losses from the battle gave the British numerical supremacy in the region. Also called the Battle of Niagara Falls, for 10 points, name this bloody battle from the War of 1812 named after a road.

text: One of this man's Secretaries of the Navy, Smith Thompson, would later become his only appointment to the Supreme Court. This man and Pinkney name a failed treaty that attempted to rework Jay's Treaty and he accompanied Robert Livingston to negotiate the Louisiana Purchase. This president saw the Fort Scott Massacre, which was resolved later by Treaty of Moultrie Creek and this man also vetoed the Cumberland Road Bill. Other than George Washington, this man was the only U.S. President to run unopposed and he defeated the last Federalist candidate for President, Rufus King, in his first presidential campaign. This man's presidency saw the signing of treaty that demilitarized the Great Lakes area, the Rush-Bagot Treaty, and his secretary of state, John Adams brokered that an eponymous agreement that purchase Florida from Spain. Presiding over the Era of Good Feelings for ten points, name this fifth US president who had a name-sake Doctrine.

text: One member of this family debated Theodore Beza at the colloquy at Poissy in 1561. Another member of this family formed a triumvirate with the Marshal de Saint-Andre and Anne de Montmorency and fought at the Battle of Dreux. The Prince de Conde and La Renaudie were unsuccessful in their attempt to attack this family in the Conspiracy of Amboise. One member of this family was known as "The Scarred" and led the Holy League. This family was largely responsible for the attempted assassination of Gaspar de Coligny, which triggered the St. Bartholomew's Day massacre. Including such members as the mother of Mary, Queen of Scots, Claude and Henry, for 10 points, name this family prominent during the French Wars of Religion.
